value.text: Portrét Benjamina Franklina od [[Joseph Duplessis|Josepha Siffreda Duplessise]] (cca 1785)
Retrat de Benjamin Franklin per Joseph Duplessis (1785).
On account of his curious Experiments and Observations on Electricity.

Deism plays a role in the founding of the American republic as well. Many of the founding fathers (Jefferson, Franklin, Madison, Paine) author statements or tracts that are sympathetic to deism; and their deistic sympathies influence the place given (or not given) to religion in the new American state that they found.

By the end of the 18th century, Deism had become a dominant religious attitude among intellectual and upper-class Americans. Benjamin Franklin, the great sage of the colonies and then of the new republic, summarized in a letter to Ezra Stiles, president of Yale College, a personal creed that almost literally reproduced Herbert’s five fundamental beliefs.
